nodes.dowod.text.t: The hetman listens to the end, and when the recording stops he says nothing for a long while. "She said 'client'. About me." He brushes the lead figures aside with his hand as if sweeping off dust. "I was right about one thing: the war was somebody's idea. Just not mine."

nodes.namiot.options.[dowod].text.t: I have a recording from the glass. Listen to it.

nodes.namiot.options.[pycha].text.t: They say the war was your idea.

nodes.namiot.options.[ton_przetarg].text.t: Someone is trading in your men, Hetman. I want to know who.

nodes.namiot.options.[ton_wyrok].text.t: I came to finish the Being and those who stand with it.

nodes.namiot.options.[ton_zwloka].text.t: There are things left unfinished, Hetman. Help me finish them.

nodes.namiot.options.[urzadzenie].text.t: What do you know about the contraption on Bald Rock?

nodes.namiot.text.t: The hetman's tent smells of tar, salt and new iron. Skjeldomir sits behind a table with a map on which lead soldiers stand in rows like on parade. "A stranger from the mainland, no colours on you. Wsiewłod sends your sort when the war stops paying him. Sit."

nodes.ton_przetarg.text.t: "Trading I understand. If someone's selling me or my men, I want to know the price. Because if it's low, I'll be insulted twice over."

nodes.ton_wyrok.text.t: Skjeldomir raises his eyes, and something shows in them that wasn't there before: attention. "Finish. That's a word I understand. You talk like a man who has already decided. Good. So have I, only I'd like to know who it's about."

nodes.ton_zwloka.text.t: "Finish. Which means something started long ago and nobody put out the light. Fine. We'll finish it, only tell me first what's left."

nodes.urzadzenie.text.t: "Bald Rock? Nobody goes there. Boats come back without their helmsmen, and those who did come back talk about a light in the ground. If you want to sail there, you sail on my boat, because only I have a helmsman who doesn't ask questions."

nodes.wojna.text.t: "Mine. I started it, I run it, and if somebody gave me powder and steel, that's plain neighbourly courtesy. Don't ask who. In my country you give, you don't ask."

nodes.wojna_po.text.t: "The war was supposed to be mine. Someone gave me powder and steel for it, and I never asked what for. Now I'm asking, and I think it's the one thing nobody warned me about."

nodes.wywiad_falsz.text.t: Skjeldomir stops moving the figures. "Forty men at the fort. Hauk doesn't know what you were called. He has a description and sends it to everyone, very thoroughly." He looks at you, then at the lead soldiers. "If I were sure, we wouldn't be talking. I only have a bad feeling, so we talk."

nodes.wywiad_prawda.text.t: The hetman doesn't look up from his soldiers. "He did. Somebody from the mainland sold him a wagon train for ninety groats. A great man, a cheap man." He moves a lead figure a finger's width to the left. "That's how wars are won. I don't like men like that, and I rate them anyway."

nodes.wywiad_proch.text.t: "Nine barrels of wet powder in the forward camp. I flogged the quartermaster, and he's probably the only one who did nothing." The hetman sets down his cup. "Clean, good work. Whoever he was, I'd rather have him with me. But you're asking oddly precisely."
